newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Robust Shenzhen A shares lift B index at noon.
newsitem.headline: Robust Shenzhen A shares lift B index at noon.

text.p: Shenzhen's B share index gained sharply at midday on Monday, spearheaded by solid rises on the A share market, brokers said.
Investors are snapping up domestic currency A shares after digesting Friday's news of a hike in the stock trading stamp tax to 0.5 percent from 0.3 percent, brokers said.
The hard currency B share index put on 4.18 points or 2.33 percent to 183.80 on turnover of HK$90.5 million.
The A index jumped 18.71 points or 3.56 percent to 543.85, with turnover reaching 10.9 billion yuan.
"The A share market rose because the stamp tax hike has been the government's only measure recently to cool down the market," an analyst at Shenzhen J&A Securities said.
"People really do not care about the 0.2 percentage points rise in a bullish stock market," the analyst said.
The B shares are likely to extend gains if the A share market continues to surge, analysts said.
But the market is vulnerable to further government intervention, although market fundamentals are favourable for buying, they said.
Jiangling Motors was the morning's best performing B share with a gain of HK$0.39 or 9.95 percent to HK$4.31.
On the A share market, refrigerator maker Changsha Zhongyi was at 6.56 yuan at noon, gaining 0.60 yuan at its 10 percent limit-up.
